A.explanation: Speeds are only swapped in the special case of equal masses with one body initially stationary, not for any two bodies.

B.explanation: Simultaneous conservation of momentum and kinetic energy in a perfectly elastic collision requires approach speed to equal separation speed.

C.explanation: A perfectly elastic collision conserves total kinetic energy as well as momentum; reduced kinetic energy describes an inelastic collision.

D.explanation: Neither body has to stop even instantaneously; both can keep moving before, during and after the collision.

hints: Notice the words perfectly elastic and must be correct for any two bodies travelling on the same straight line.
Recall what perfectly elastic means: total momentum is conserved and total kinetic energy is also conserved, with no loss to heat or deformation.
Test each statement for unequal masses: check whether speeds must swap, whether kinetic energy must fall, and whether relative speed of approach $v_1 - v_2$ must match relative speed of separation.
walkthrough: Identify the given situation: two bodies moving along the same line collide and the collision is perfectly elastic.
State the governing rules: for any collision with no external impulse total momentum is conserved, and perfectly elastic adds that total kinetic energy $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$ is also conserved.
Combine the two conservation equations for masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ with velocities before $u_1, u_2$ and after $v_1, v_2$; the algebra gives $|u_1 - u_2| = |v_1 - v_2|$.
Interpret the result: the magnitude of the relative speed of approach before impact equals the magnitude of the relative speed of separation after impact.

Check the other statements: speed swapping needs equal masses, kinetic energy is not reduced in elastic impact, and momentary rest is only a special case. Therefore the always-true property is equal approach and separation speeds. This is option B.
